title: fix(automation,metadata-protocol,rest,spec): a stored flow the engine refuses is served beside its verdict, not as running
body:
Fixes #23316
Clause-②: yes (the flow meta read and list gain a read-time field: the engine's verdict on a stored flow)

## What changes

A stored flow the automation engine refuses is no longer served as running. The stored row's `status` stays exactly as authored; the engine's verdict is served beside the item:

- **Item read**, both branches of `GET /api/v1/meta/flow/NAME`:
  - uncached (`getMetaItem`): a new envelope key `registration`, a sibling of `lock`;
  - the DEFAULT cached branch (`metadata.enableCache: true`): the same `registration`, read live on every call (claim amendment `6157354342`).
- **List** (`getMetaItems` / `GET /api/v1/meta/flow`): a new top-level key `registrations`, keyed by flow name, beside `items`. The REST list chain keeps sibling keys (`withItems` spreads the protocol's envelope), so both transports serve it.

The closed state set is the one the engine can actually answer, total over its state for a name:

| `state` | When |
|:---|:---|
| `registered` | the engine holds a registration under the name |
| `refused` | the engine's last attempt to register the stored flow threw and it holds nothing under the name; `reason` = the thrown error's own `message`, and its string `code` only when the error set one (verbatim, never paraphrased, never invented) |
| `unregistered` | the engine holds nothing and recorded no refusal (a read during boot, between a save and the engine following it, or after a deliberate unregister) |

`refused` requires `reason` (a discriminated union), so a refused verdict without its reason does not parse.

**An unjudged flow reads the field as ABSENT, not as a third state.** The field is the engine's answer or nothing. Where no automation service declares the member (a control-plane or metadata-only host), the protocol has no engine to ask, and a protocol-minted `unknown` would be a verdict nobody made. Both schema members document absence as "no engine judged it, never `registered`". The same absence applies to every type other than `flow`, to draft reads (a pending body is not what the engine holds), and to the execution face the engine binds from.

## The seam (the claim's premise, verified before any edit)

The protocol reads the verdict through the kernel's service table by name — `this.getServicesRegistry?.().get('automation')` — resolved lazily per call. Precedent: `resolveFlowCanonicalizer` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`), which reads `canonicalizeStoredFlow` from the same service the same way, for the save door and the stored migration. The member is declared on the existing contract `IAutomationService` in `@objectstack/spec/contracts` (`getFlowRegistration?(name)`, optional, beside `canonicalizeStoredFlow` and `getFlowRuntimeStates`), which `AutomationEngine` implements; the automation plugin registers the engine itself under `automation`. `metadata-protocol` imports nothing from `service-automation`.

The REST cached branch reaches the same seam through the protocol. `getMetaItemCached` already performs the uncached read on every call (it is a validator wrapper, not a store), so it returns that read's live `registration` beside `data`. `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema` declares it, and `rest-server.ts` spreads it into the cached envelope for `flow` only.

## The default cached branch: live, not stored, not in the ETag

- `getMetaItemCached` hashes the document alone, as before. The verdict is not stored anywhere and is never part of the ETag.
- **Consequence, and the reason for it:** a cached read that carries `registration` is never answered `304 Not Modified`. The protocol's own invariant at that validator says a 304 may be answered only on an exact match over the bytes actually sent. With the verdict outside the hash, a 304 would pin the caller to the verdict it was served before. That happens when the engine re-registers or refuses the flow under an unchanged body, for example on a restart with a different plugin set, or when the post-save sync lands after the first read. Answering in full costs only the saved body bytes, since the method performs the delegate read either way (the same trade `rest-server.ts` records for `dashboard`). An unjudged flow (no automation service) keeps its 304 exactly as before.
- Every other type's cached envelope is byte-identical (pinned).

## Where the verdict is recorded (`service-automation`)

- **The `kernel:ready` cold-boot bind** records each refused name with what the engine threw, after the withdrawal. The withdrawal itself, the warn line and its level are unchanged.
- **The `metadata:reloaded` re-sync** and **the metadata-change sync** (a save, publish, delete, revert at runtime) record a refusal that leaves the name unregistered. A refused re-registration of a name the engine still holds leaves the old registration in place (`registerFlow` throws before it changes anything), so that name stays `registered`.
- **Not recorded: the boot pull** in `start()`. The bind re-judges every flow of the view at `kernel:ready`, so a record made there is a verdict this same boot can contradict (AGENTS.md "Startup registry reads"). `check:startup-registry-verdict` is green.
- **Cleared** by a later successful `registerFlow` of the name and by `withdrawFlow`. `recordFlowRefusal` ignores a name the engine holds, so a name is never `refused` and registered at once.

## Multi-process

The verdict is the engine of the process that answered the read; no cross-process store is consulted. The schema members and the docs page (`content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`, "Discovery & Registration") say so.

## Tests

- `packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts` (new): the triage pin over the real composition (ObjectKernel, ObjectQLPlugin's metadata protocol on driver-sql / better-sqlite3 in memory, the real automation plugin).
  - Setup: two stored `sys_metadata` flow rows land after ObjectQL started, so the boot pull never sees them. The node type's executor registers from a later plugin's `start()` (the #21848 harness shape), so the `kernel:ready` bind refuses the row whose plugin node carries an undeclared key.
  - The item read serves `item.status === 'active'` beside `registration: { state: 'refused', reason: { message } }`. The message equals what `registerFlow` throws for that body, with no `code` (a plain error).
  - The cached read, the producer behind the default door, carries the same refusal and `registered` for the control.
  - Control: the registered row reads `{ state: 'registered' }`, its status as stored.
  - The list carries both verdicts in `registrations`, keyed by name, with the items bare.
  - A corrected save clears the refusal (`registered`).
- `packages/rest/src/meta-flow-cached-registration.test.ts` (new): the default door.
  - Asserted on the cached branch (`getMetaItemCached` called, `getMetaItem` not).
  - A refused flow: the stored status unchanged, `registration: refused` with its reason beside it.
  - Control: a registered flow's cached body is exactly `{ type, name, item, registration: registered }`.
  - Control: another type's cached envelope is exactly what it was.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.flow-by-name-shipped-name.test.ts`: nine cases on that file's already-pinned engine double (its `harness` gains an optional service table).
  - The engine's answer passed through beside `lock`, never inside `item`.
  - Absent with no automation service, and with one that declares no member.
  - Absent for `view`, and the engine is never asked.
  - Absent on a draft read.
  - The list is keyed by name, a loader's flow included. The execution face carries none. A pending draft gets no entry.
  - The cached read carries the verdict with an ETag equal to the unjudged read's.
  - A judged cached read is never answered 304; the unjudged control still is.
- `packages/spec/src/api/meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts`:
  - compile-time pins: `registration` is the verdict or undefined; `registrations` is a name-keyed record of verdicts or undefined;
  - the three states parse; a fourth state and a reason-less `refused` are refused; absence stays absent.
- `packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`: the two new schemas are pinned isomorphic (ADR-0122), count 776 to 778. `packages/spec/variant-docs.json` binds the three states to the flows page (`check:variant-docs`).

**Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, wrap mode, subject imported from source in both, so no `dist/` sits on the path):

1. **Engine record.** The bind's `recordFlowRefusal` call was replaced by a marker comment: anchor 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1, blob `29d687232ea8` to `cba906b7c690`.
   - The pin went red, 2 failed / 2 passed: the refused item read answered `{ state: 'unregistered' }`, and so did the list entry.
   - Restored: blob == HEAD `29d687232ea8`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
   - A first attempt was a no-op (the tool refused a replacement that was a substring of the anchor; nothing ran) and is not counted.
2. **REST spread.** The cached envelope's `...cachedRegistration` was replaced by a marker comment: blob `41d526941b28` to `0e5e6328b07b`.
   - The REST pin went red, 2 failed / 1 passed: the refused read had no `registration`, and the registered control lost it. The other-type control stayed green.
   - Restored: blob == HEAD `41d526941b28`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Verification (local, shared box; CI runs the full battery)

Final head `2b84fe555` = this branch merged with `origin/main` `6d96721fa` through `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`. PRs #23315 and #23311 landed in that range, and nothing conflicted. `check:generated` reported all 14 artifacts up to date after the rebuild.

- **Typecheck, final head:** `@objectstack/spec` (tsc, scripts, test layer), `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation` (and its test layer), `@objectstack/rest` (and its test layer). All exit 0.
- **Derived gates, final head:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran` (exit-annotated record) printed: "Run reconciliation — 116 derived, 114 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN". All 114 exit 0. The two NOT MEASURED families:
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET. It reads every workspace package's `dist/`, and a full `pnpm build` was not run on the shared box.
  - `check:type-check-debt`: its `--re-measure` rebuilds and type-checks the whole workspace, past the foreground cap. A first attempt was cap-killed and left half-built `dist/`s in this worktree, which were rebuilt before `check:dts-closure` was re-run green.
- **Full suites, all green** (sharded under `os-verify-lock`):
  - on `8f39c942f` (after the first main merge, before the cached-branch widening): `@objectstack/service-automation` 186 files / 2453 tests; `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` 238 files / 28339 tests (+19 skipped); `@objectstack/spec` (local project) 669 files / 20278 tests;
  - on `9c498cda5` (after the widening): `@objectstack/rest` (local project) 280 files / 5839 tests (+326 skipped), plus the five `getMetaItemCached` files of `metadata-protocol`, 132 tests.
- **Re-run on the final head** (declared narrowing; CI runs the full suites on the merged head):
  - the pin files above;
  - every test file `origin/main` changed in these four packages: 55 + 94 + 27 + 20 tests;
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test:repo`: 58 of 59 files green (35 tree-scoped pins / 474 tests; 21 script suites / 425; 2 publish-smoke / 24).
  - NOT MEASURED: `scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts`. Run alone, it passed 35 tests and was then cut at the 7.5-minute foreground cap under lock contention. Left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope findings, not filed (the seat decides):

- **The default cached branch still serves no protection envelope** (`lock`, `version`, `editable`, `deletable`, `resettable`, provenance). This is pre-existing and already declared in `GetMetaItemResponseSchema`'s docblock, which leaves it open (the sweep of #5950). Per the amendment it is not this card's. Carrier: the `domain:spec` seat.
- **objectui (H5), measured read-only at `7578323`.** No console surface reads the new `registration`. Today a refused flow shows as:
  - `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx:6412`: the open flow's runtime row comes from `GET /api/v1/automation/_status`. A refused flow has no engine row (`null`), so the header pill and the Problems panel read `unpublished` ("Unpublished draft", amber). That is the wrong reason, though not "running".
  - The same file at `:5700` (`FlowStatusDot`): no row means no dot on the rail.
  - `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/flow-problems.ts:375` (`deriveFlowRunStatus`): with no runtime reading (no provider, or `_status` not read yet) it falls back to the stored `status`, so a refused `active` flow renders `enabled`.
  - Carrier: the seat files the objectui follow-up.
- **Read from source only, not reproduced through a public door.** The metadata-change sync and the reload re-sync warn "the engine keeps the registration it had" when a changed flow is refused. If the save door accepts a body `registerFlow` then refuses, the engine runs the older body while the read serves the newer one beside `registration: registered`. Whether a door accepts such a body was not measured. Carrier: none.
- **Tooling observation.** `pnpm check:type-check-debt` runs unlocked as a `check:*` gate, but its `--re-measure` builds workspace `dist/`s. When cap-killed mid-run, it leaves packages with JS deleted and declarations stale (`tsup` clean). Carrier: none.

Dedupe words: flow registration verdict meta read; refused flow registration served beside status; cached meta item branch missing envelope lock version.
